newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on local demand, fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on local demand, fall seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Friday as local operators started buying at new lower levels, but traders forecast a downside correction in the next few days as foreign investors did not support the move.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 leading shares rose 2.33 percent to 473.12, on moderate total market turnover of $49.12 million.

"The market nudged up, but it is not a change of a trend, the trend is a downside one," said Rinaco Plus trader Valery Levit. "It is unlikely to have a push up from these levels. A new rally is unlikely to happen before mid-August."
UES power utility rose to $0.4165 from $0.4130, Irkutskenergo power utility edged up to $0.336 from $0.0.300 and LUKoil rose to $21.19 from $20.70.
Russian share prices have been slipping in a correction for several days with occasional rises after an almost 30 percent rise last month.
"Today was the swan song of the summer rally," said Prospekt corporate securties director Andrei Ippolitov. "There is likely to be a turning point next week."
He said most foreign investors, who make the greatest impact on the local market, had already exhausted their summer limits for Russia.
Russian buyers attacked blue chips aggressively in the morning as they thought prices had hit bottom, Levit said. But foreigners operators did not support them, and started selling leading shares.
He said he saw foreign and Russian demand in second-tier shares, which had lagged behind leading stocks in the rise.
Oil companies Megionneftegaz rose to $8.50 from $7.60 and Kondpetroleum was $2.20 after $1.70. Kubanenergo power utility rose to $0.735 from $0.715.

Oil company Yuganskneftegaz edged down to $29.10 from $31.50. The stock has been rising strongly in the last few days as its capital/reserves ratio was better than other second-tier oil shares, Levit said.
